summary: The National Education Association urges the FCC to preserve the E-Rate program, opposing any proposal to reduce or sunset it, emphasizing the program's ongoing importance for connectivity and equity. The NEA argues that the FCC cannot sunset E-Rate, as Congress did not authorize it to do so, and that the program is necessary for continuous connectivity support. The NEA also contends that connectivity is not a one-time asset but an ongoing operational cost that requires sustained support. The NEA opposes limiting E-Rate eligibility scope to narrow eligible equipment and services, arguing that it would restrict access to necessary broadband for schools and libraries. The comment emphasizes the importance of context-dependent screen use in education and argues against treating all screen use as uniformly negative. It highlights the need to consider the educational purpose and professional judgment of educators when making E-Rate decisions. The comment also points out the administrative burden and cost implications of imposing new requirements on schools, particularly those serving young children.
